convention: This file carries POINTERS AND TRAPS, not retellings. A задача is cited by its section in PLAN.md or SPEC.md, never paraphrased here: a paraphrase is a second copy of the truth and it drifts (it already did once, for routing_lists). What belongs here instead: file and symbol pointers, measured facts, rejected shapes with their arguments, and the traps that cost the last passes time. Written down in full in implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое'.

citation_hygiene.rule: Every path, T/W number, policy name and git ref named in this file must exist. This is no longer a convention a human has to remember — `go run ./cmd/doclint .` checks it, and CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .`.
citation_hygiene.why_this_block_still_exists: It records what the check is FOR. Two consecutive passes cited 'Global Constraint 9, constraints.md' — a file that never existed in any branch — and the citation was what justified deferring a task that, when finally checked on its merits, cost one optional field and one wiring line. The rule that citation stood in for: a pass closes its own queue item and does not widen into neighbouring modules; where the correct shape does require changing another package, that is recorded in Deviations with an argument — it is not grounds to defer the task silently.

closed_this_pass.old_flags: The six Р40 flags are REMOVED, not aliased (PLAN.md stage 9: two interfaces to one store drift apart). The price is paid out loud: the retiredFlags table answers `-sub` with 'снят … теперь `hop sub add <url>`' on stderr and exit 1 — measured live by the controller.
closed_this_pass.exit_codes: One codeFor() function, not os.Exit by site. 0 done; 2 the background half is absent (ipc.Connect refused); 3 no live nodes (§5.6); 1 everything else, INCLUDING a broken settings.json — a configuration fault is not fail-close (W57). Code 3 is not faked: it is observable today only on `probe`, which measures liveness through the product's own engine and prober (§6.7); a node at 127.0.0.1:1 produces it without network or privileges. Verified live by the controller: probe → 3, probe --json → 3 with parseable JSON, status without a service → 2, empty store → 1.
closed_this_pass.json: emit(out, view, asJSON) in cmd/hop/output.go is the only place encoding/json runs; one value per command, two renderings. Guarded three ways: schema by literals (a renamed field goes red instead of migrating into the expectation), one-formation-point by AST (a json.Marshal outside emit is a finding — the W29 device), and every reading command accepting --json.
closed_this_pass.measured_not_assumed: `hop probe --json` printed Xray's own WebSocket-deprecation warning to STDOUT before the JSON, so the machine output did not parse. `loglevel: none` does not silence it — the warning predates the instance. Fixed in internal/engine (the owner of Xray) by takeXrayLogOffStdout; guarded by a test that swaps the real os.Stdout for a pipe. No schema check could ever have seen this: they look at the value, the garbage arrives in the stream.
closed_this_pass.controller_correction: specVerbs was a literal copy of the §5.9 verb list inside the test, so the spec could drift from the grammar silently. It is now parsed out of SPEC.md (the `hop a | b | c` line inside §5.9, found via negcheck.ModuleRoot); a missing section or line is a failure, not an empty list. Negative control in all three directions: an extra verb in §5.9, a verb removed from §5.9, and the enumeration line deleted.
closed_this_pass.honest_gaps: `hop status` shows only the service phase: traffic phase and active node belong to the agent, and the store holds an exclusive flock for its whole life (measured live: a held .lock makes `hop nodes` wait 5s and refuse with code 1), so a status command that opens the store would refuse exactly when it is most needed. An always-empty field would read as 'no traffic', which is a lie — the command says in words what it does not know.

parallel_passes_trap.what_was_done_this_time: The controller handed out the numbers BEFORE the passes started (W51 to the idle sweep, W52-W53 to the lists, W54 kept for its own pass) and required each number to stand in the test NAME. No collision occurred. Repeat this: it is the cheap half.
parallel_passes_trap.what_the_zones_did_not_catch: Every merge conflict of the four passes landed in exactly three places, and a next parallel run should expect them: the tail of the §5.8 table, the flag table in §6, and the tail of implementation-notes.md. Two more shapes cost a minute each: the §6.1 line that counted the green numbers (now deleted, so it can no longer conflict), and a heading level — pass sections in implementation-notes.md are `###`, and a pass that writes `##` is not wrong enough to notice on its own.
parallel_passes_trap.rule_for_the_next_parallel_run: Hand out registry numbers in advance and require them in test names; name the zones per-file; and expect to resolve document tails by hand — that part is the controller's job, not a defect of the split.
parallel_passes_trap.what_the_controller_had_to_check_by_hand: Both passes of this round shipped a test that looked like a guard and was not: one compared goroutine COUNTS (green with the mechanism commented out), the other compared the grammar against a COPY of the spec's verb list. Neither was caught by any gate command — a green test is indistinguishable from a vacuous one until you break the mechanism on purpose. Do that on every incoming test whose subject is 'the thing exists': comment the mechanism out and demand red.

The same absence is why `hop status` knows only the tunnel phase (the agent holds the store's flock, so no other process can read the store while the tunnel is up), why exit code 3 is observable only on `probe`, and why the `event_broadcast` policy still has no code (docs/not-yet-written.md).

notes.doclint: Fast. Runs in CI as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 46 policies as of this pass, ~25-35 min wall clock on this machine — this is expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. Per-task gate only needs the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name>; the controller runs the full one at the end.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: Build once, run under an unprivileged user namespace: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). This works without root — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN inside the fresh netns. Reusing the built binary across repeated unshare invocations is much faster than `go test` per run.
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). `go run ./cmd/realtimelint .` is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. `gofmt -l ./internal` reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code.
